features.text: The patient injured his right knee approximately two and a half weeks ago.
The injury occurred when the patient turned his ankle while stepping off a curb.
The patient experiences clicking in the right knee.
The patient sometimes feels locked in the right knee when resting it on his heel for too long.
The patient is worried the injury might be something more serious.
The patient had an x-ray of the right knee, which did not show any acute fracture or bony abnormality.
The patient has no prior history of knee injuries, meniscal tears, ligament damage, or knee surgery.
The clicking sensation occurs on the outside of the right knee, especially during a full squat.
The patient can bend and straighten his knee without difficulty.
The locking sensation worsens when resting the foot on the heel for an extended time, such as leaning against a wall.
The locking sensation does not significantly interfere with daily tasks, except during gardening or bending down.
The clicking and locking occur on the lateral aspect of the right knee, especially during a full squat or when resting the foot on the heel.
The patient experiences mild pain when the doctor pulls his foot to the outside during the exam.
The patient has not undergone an MRI of the right knee.
The patient has no swelling, tenderness, or instability in the right knee, except for mild pain during the exam.
The patient does not feel warmth or swelling around the right knee.
The patient does not experience episodes of the knee giving way or buckling during normal movement.
